claim: Five September paired AES-128 study sessions contain 6000 retained encryption observations.
qualification: Five processes on one hardware pair; warmups provenance-supported, not retained.

claim: Baseline pipeline is slower than the allocating CPU AES-NI transform in every session at 1/16/32 MiB.
qualification: Prepared host-memory pipeline; no claim about total CPU capacity.

claim: GPU H2D and D2H host intervals and pipeline kernel events were recorded.
qualification: Copy intervals include synchronization; transfer sum is computed.

claim: The historical CPU factory explicitly requests AES-NI and dispatch is checked outside timing.
qualification: Native initialization, not instruction tracing.

claim: The application executes one synchronous CPU encryption call with serial orchestration.
qualification: Supports single-stream/application-level serial wording only.

claim: CPU output allocation is timed; GPU pinning, staging, buffers and key setup are excluded.
qualification: Scopes are asymmetric; prepared in-memory comparison only.

claim: Payload sizes are binary and throughput decimal; measurements encrypt only.
qualification: CTR has no authentication.

claim: All nine supplied manuscript throughput values reconstruct at one decimal.
qualification: Median of five session throughput medians, not reciprocal median time.

claim: Rate-based pipeline price thresholds at 1/16/32 MiB are 0.950326/0.762598/0.827330.
qualification: Unrounded aggregate throughput ratio; not session-paired speedup.

claim: Paired-time pipeline thresholds are 0.952927/0.749551/0.823251.
qualification: Median across five CPU-median/GPU-median time ratios; report session ranges.

claim: Combined pipeline non-kernel fractions can be derived using the same-pipeline event component.
qualification: Mixed clock residual; not pure PCIe, allocation, energy or utilization.

claim: Seconds per decimal GB are 1000/R for repeated batches at the measured rate.
qualification: Not a measured contiguous 1 GB request or long-running service test.

claim: CPU hourly cost is 1 normalized unit and GPU ratios are .50/.75/1/1.25/1.50/2.
qualification: No EUR/USD, market observation or power assumption.

claim: Variable charge is proportional to occupied time, using consistent resource attribution.
qualification: Include GPU host allocation; minimum billing, utilization and capacity are outside model.

claim: A linear fixed-plus-variable cost model defines a break-even candidate.
qualification: No empirical fixed costs, volume or period; feasible positive V* not established.

claim: Under equal hourly charge and nonnegative GPU fixed premium, baseline large-batch pipeline has no positive break-even.
qualification: Conditional conclusion; does not establish actual procurement cost.

claim: Later Windows EVP and Oracle one/two-worker studies exist and validate.
qualification: Different implementation and operation scopes; never replace historical CPU.

claim: T4 page prepared-pipeline/EVP comparison favors CPU transform at all four batch sizes in all five sessions.
qualification: Different campaign and independent-page semantics; ratio direction CPU time/GPU time below one.

claim: Three later platform studies have retained complete validated evidence.
qualification: Existing numerical audit reused after checking all 405 referenced artifact hashes; no pooling.

claim: The historical CPU benchmark measures aggregate multicore capacity.
qualification: Reject: single-stream measurements cannot estimate total CPU capacity.

claim: All native execution was independently confirmed single-threaded and pinned to one core.
qualification: Reject: no native thread trace or affinity restriction.

claim: The GIL proves the native AES function uses one thread.
qualification: Reject: native FFI GIL release and native concurrency are separate questions.

claim: GPU throughput proves superior energy efficiency.
qualification: Reject: no integrated validated CPU/GPU energy data.

claim: GPU is cheaper at actual market prices or yields positive investment ROI.
qualification: Reject: prices, fixed costs, utilization and capacity scenario not supplied.

claim: GPU E2E measures complete business-application latency.
qualification: Reject: excluded setup/staging/I/O/authentication/orchestration.

claim: Pipeline minus separately measured resident time is measured PCIe transfer time.
qualification: Reject: independent executions/scopes, synchronization, launch and mixed clocks.

claim: Baseline/v1 CUDA represents highly optimized production AES.
qualification: Reject: educational candidates, no tuning/side-channel/production claim.

claim: AES-128 CTR encryption results establish authenticated secure application throughput.
qualification: Reject: unauthenticated CTR; no authentication overhead measured.

claim: Results generalize to all CPU/GPU platforms, cloud prices or operating systems.
qualification: Reject: primary one local pair, later heterogeneous contexts not controlled causal interventions.

claim: The 16 MiB dip is caused by PCIe, thermals or a library version.
qualification: Reject: fixed size order and confounded hardware/software; retain observed dip.

claim: A two-worker ARM result replaces Windows multicore AES-NI data.
qualification: Reject: platform, implementation and scope differ.

claim: Five sessions and 100 repetitions establish population significance or independent machines.
qualification: Reject: repetitions nested within five sessions on one platform.

claim: The proposed study is novel and has no prior-publication overlap.
qualification: Unknown: authors must disclose reused data; repository absence is not novelty evidence.

claim: The normalized linear model is empirically measured TCO.
qualification: Reject: only conditional resource charges; fixed costs and business factors absent.
